title: U.S. intelligence chief says Megaspeed and Alice Huang are under investigation as a new figure emerges in the Nvidia chip case
summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the U.S. is investigating Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, CNBC reported on November 23, 2026. Alice Huang, with whom ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly had a romantic relationship, was a key figure at the Singapore-based cloud firm, which runs data centers across Southeast Asia. “There is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her,” Clayton told ABC on Sunday. “Nvidia chips, they are the jewel. They are the absolute top that everybody wants, that's why we're focusing on this.” The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday that her associate Li Ming, a Chinese national out on bail in Singapore, was “deeply involved” in Megaspeed’s major decisions; his Singapore charges concern alleged false representations to Super Micro Computer. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration wants answers about who at Nvidia oversaw compliance on chip sales to China. Jensen Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter have agreed to closed-door interviews with three House committees on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2. Megaspeed says it is a “legitimate and lawful business.”

title: Oregon and Virginia become the first states to sue SpaceX over Grok deepfake images
summary: Virginia and Oregon have become the first states to sue Elon Musk’s SpaceX over its Grok AI image generator, CNBC reported on November 23, 2026. In separate state-court complaints, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argue SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X users from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material, and falsely represented Grok and X as generally safe in violation of state consumer-protection laws. “This content can cause fear, distress, and anxiety in those who are unwillingly exposed to the content,” Jones wrote. Both states seek injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs; Virginia also seeks restitution for consumers. Oregon filed in Multnomah County Circuit Court on Sunday evening and Virginia in the City of Richmond Circuit Court on Monday morning, and as of early Monday both suits were pending the courts’ acceptance. SpaceX, which already faces other Grok-related suits and probes worldwide, did not immediately respond to CNBC’s request for comment.

title: OpenAI’s chief scientist proposes perplexity as the yardstick for an AI speed limit
summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has published a blog post on how to put limits on AI development, centered on a measurement called perplexity, TechCrunch reported on November 22, 2026. The debate over slowing AI has intensified since Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a plan to “pace the frontier,” calling for “common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.” But a speed limit needs a speedometer. Pachocki argues that benchmarks focused on AI’s “downstream capabilities” quickly go stale, while perplexity, which “measures how well a model predicts the next token on average,” has stayed “informative.” His post charts how OpenAI models’ perplexity has fallen since GPT-3.5. “Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics,” he wrote. Under his idea, companies would commit not to pass a set threshold “until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone.” Sam Altman called the post “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while.”

title: Intelligence chief warns of more tech-outage ‘bumps in the road’ as systems upgrade for the AI age
summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for “bumps in the road” after damaging technology outages hit air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook, CNBC reported on November 22, 2026. Officials have largely dismissed the idea that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, stem from a coordinated or AI cyberattack. But Clayton told CNN’s “State of the Union” that disruptions may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems. Americans “should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road,” he said. The warning comes ahead of one of the year’s busiest travel weeks. The FAA said router upgrades caused the data flood behind a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago, and Microsoft blamed its Outlook outage on “an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade.” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS that bank patches may cause glitches: “I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency.”

title: Walmart opens its site to Meta’s Muse agent for Black Friday shopping
summary: Walmart will let Meta’s Muse AI agent find and buy Black Friday deals on its website on shoppers’ behalf, The Verge reported on November 23, 2026. The retailer is rolling out a live version of the Agent Gateway it announced last month, which helps AI agents find relevant products without sharing your purchase history. Walmart told The Verge after publication that the launch slipped by 24 hours, so shopping via Muse will now be available on Tuesday, November 24. Purchases run through Walmart “Agent Profiles,” a dedicated space for agent activity inside a customer’s account where you can set spending limits, approve purchases and check everything Muse has bought. Checkout happens inside the conversation using a card saved to your Walmart account, at the same prices as Walmart.com, and Walmart’s return policy still applies. While other online retailers like Amazon and eBay have blocked AI agents from browsing their platforms, Walmart says Muse support is “just the beginning,” with experiences for other agents and apps “on the way.”

title: S&P 500 futures jump 2.4% as a shortened Thanksgiving week opens after the tech rout
summary: U.S. stock futures bounced as a holiday-shortened week got underway after all three major averages ended Friday in correction territory, CNBC reported in its live markets coverage dated November 22, 2026. Futures tied to the Dow gained 853 points, or 1.8%, S&P 500 futures added 2.4%, and Nasdaq-100 futures rose 3%. Nvidia soared 6% in premarket trading after President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post that he hopes Nvidia’s board rehires Jensen Huang as CEO; Micron added 4%, AMD 3% and CoreWeave 5%. Last week was the worst weekly decline for the Nasdaq Composite and Dow in more than six years and the largest for the S&P 500 since April 2025, leaving the Nasdaq negative for the year. Roundhill’s Drew Pettit said the indiscriminate selling late in the week may signal the sell-off is ending. “Fundamentally, I think the floor is a lot higher,” he said. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday’s session closes early at 1:00 p.m.

title: Nvidia climbs 8.76% in premarket trading as Big Tech bounces after the Nasdaq’s worst week since 2020
summary: Nvidia and Anthropic shares rose in premarket trading Monday after AI stocks fell in the Nasdaq’s worst week since 2020, CNBC reported on November 23, 2026. Nvidia rose 8.76%, following a more than 40% slump over the past month as Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO of the company he founded after admitting to an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Anthropic was up 4.38% at 6:45 a.m. ET, ahead of its third day of trading; it gained 17% in Thursday’s debut before closing 8.5% down on Friday, after raising a record $93.5 billion in its IPO and an additional $26 billion from tech giants that bought at the offer price. Other Big Tech names were buoyed too: Alphabet rose 6%, Meta added 4.29%, Amazon was up 3.92%, Microsoft jumped 3.66%, AMD added 4.84% and SpaceX was up 3.18%. Neoclouds also showed signs of recovery. The Nasdaq slid 10% last week, and CNBC noted investors remain nervous about some AI companies’ valuations and business models.

title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal
summary: CrowdStrike said Monday it will buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valuing the network-security company at about $43.9 billion, one of the largest cybersecurity deals on record, CNBC reported on November 23, 2026. Zscaler shares jumped more than 13% in premarket trading, while CrowdStrike fell over 8%. Zscaler shareholders will get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share, implying $260.41 per Zscaler share, a 34% premium to its last close, and CrowdStrike holders will own about 84% of the combined company. The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike’s fiscal 2028. CEO George Kurtz will lead the combined company, while Zscaler’s Jay Chaudhry will keep running the Zscaler business and join CrowdStrike’s board. CNBC tied the deal to AI adoption raising cyber risks by helping attackers find and exploit software weaknesses faster. CrowdStrike says the combination expands its total addressable market by more than $185 billion and creates a company with more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue at closing. Zscaler’s first-quarter revenue rose 20% to $949.3 million.

title: ASML rebounds 3.48% as European chip stocks lead a modest recovery
summary: ASML shares rose 3.48% to €1,208.60 at 9:04 a.m. CET on Monday, leading a modest European stock rebound after last week’s AI-driven sell-off, Chip Dispatch reported on November 23, 2026. The pan-European Stoxx 600 stood 0.29% higher at 627.44 at the same time, citing CNBC quote data, and German chipmaker Infineon gained 2.23% to €46.46. Software maker SAP fell 1.21% to €181.46, which made semiconductors rather than software the session’s clearest source of upward momentum. National benchmarks moved in a narrow band: Germany’s DAX rose 0.37%, France’s CAC 40 gained 0.33% and London’s FTSE 100 advanced 0.10%. Financial shares also firmed, with HSBC up 1.01% and Deutsche Bank up 1.13%. The rebound followed a split Asian session in which the Kospi fell 3% and the Taiex rose 2%. Chip Dispatch described the opening as a broad advance in direction, “but not a uniform surge in magnitude.”

title: Baseten releases bison-1 and groundhog-1, open-weight models that make decisions instead of chatting
summary: Baseten has released two open-weight models built to make structured choices rather than write chat answers, Open Model Weights reported on November 22, 2026. Announced November 20, bison-1 and groundhog-1 join the Base Labs decision-model family; both accept text and images, are offered through Baseten Model APIs, and have official Hugging Face repositories exposing the weights. Baseten describes bison-1 as a dense 31-billion-parameter model built on Google Gemma 4 31B, while groundhog-1 uses the Gemma 4 26B-A4B mixture-of-experts architecture with about four billion active parameters per token. Both offer a 128K context window. Decision models evaluate explicitly defined answer choices and assign probabilities, which suits routing, prioritization and quality checks. Baseten says bison-1 scored 76 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1, ahead of 18 other evaluated decision models, with a Brier calibration score of 0.14. The checkpoints list a combination of MIT and Apache 2.0 terms. Open Model Weights says it has not reproduced the benchmark figures.

title: NeuML’s Atto shrinks search models down to as few as 840 parameters
summary: NeuML has introduced Atto, a collection of unusually compact models for embedding, ranking and related search workloads, Open Model Weights reported on November 22, 2026. In its November 19 announcement, the publisher describes a research program spanning an experimental ColBERT configuration with just 840 parameters and dense embedding checkpoints reaching 28 million parameters. The family is not one uniform model: members use different encoding approaches, sizes and embedding dimensions, with some configurations reaching 8,192 dimensions. For teams building retrieval-augmented generation or local document search, smaller encoders may cut checkpoint storage and the computation needed to produce vectors, though very wide outputs can still burden vector indexes and nearest-neighbor search, so parameter count alone is not a complete deployment metric. The model card for the inspected 28M dense variant declares Apache-2.0, but Open Model Weights says each checkpoint’s license should be verified individually. It has not reproduced NeuML’s retrieval results and calls Atto “an engineering option rather than a universal replacement for established embedding systems.”

title: Metric AI releases Ayb 0.5, open-weight language models built for Armenian
summary: Metric AI Lab has introduced Ayb 0.5, a family of Armenian-focused open-weight language models, Open Model Weights reported on November 22, 2026. The November 20 release includes Ayb-0.5-0.8B, Ayb-0.5-4B and Ayb-0.5-9B, sized for budgets from lightweight text processing to larger conversational and vision-language apps. Ayb is built on Qwen3.5 rather than trained from scratch: the developers expanded the tokenizer with Armenian vocabulary, continued pretraining on Armenian and English data, and added instruction tuning and post-training. Metric AI says the 9B version supports multi-turn conversations, complex prompts and tool calling, and it kept Qwen3.5’s vision encoder so the models can answer image-based questions in Armenian. The team reports Ayb-9B scored 0.6164 on ArmBench, ranking third in its cited evaluation, with the 4B and 0.8B at 0.5828 and 0.5300. Training emphasized Eastern Armenian, so Western Armenian and dialects are less reliable. The 9B model card lists a noncommercial CC BY-NC 4.0 license, and Open Model Weights has not independently verified the benchmarks.

title: Quantum computing’s first real-world payoff may come in energy, from steadier grids to better solar cells
summary: Quantum software is already being tested on the energy transition, from keeping power grids stable to finding better materials for solar cells and hydrogen production, CNBC reported on November 22, 2026, even as bigger promises like drug discovery remain years away. Phasecraft, founded in Bristol, England, in 2019, has partnered with Britain’s National Energy System Operator on grid tasks such as managing power exchanges and isolating network sections during emergencies, and says its software can complete them up to 1,000 times faster than conventional computing. It is also working with Oxford PV on more efficient photovoltaic materials and, with Johnson Matthey, Harvard and QuEra under ARPA-E oversight, on catalysts that reduce reliance on scarce metals like iridium. Quantinuum is modeling materials for hydrogen fuel cells, and Oxford spinout ORCA Computing has worked with BP on how biofuels burn. “When you get this right, the commercial returns are real: more efficient energy networks mean lower operating costs and more value from existing infrastructure,” said Phasecraft CEO Ashley Montanaro.

title: The vibe-coding revolution comes for your gadgets, from TVs to cameras and synths
summary: People everywhere are using AI coding tools to hack their hardware just by prompting Claude Code or Codex, The Verge’s David Pierce wrote in The Stepback on November 22, 2026. One developer in India, Gathin T, had Claude Code redesign his ad-cluttered Android TV in about an hour and a half, then launched CleanYourTV, which became one of the most popular repositories on GitHub. Camera fans are adding recording features and color profiles, musicians are turning the cheap M-Vave FM-1 synth into new gear, and one vibe coder found a way to play PlayStation 2 discs on a PlayStation 5. Hacker-friendly ESP32 modules are spreading too, letting people build hyper-specific devices for a few dollars and a few prompts. The risks are real: modded firmware usually voids warranties and can brick devices. Gathin’s advice echoes what Pierce hears from vibe hackers everywhere: never give the bots access to something you can’t afford to lose. “Even for fiddling with stuff,” he says, “I have an external computer which runs through Linux. So I just use it like a sandbox environment to test things out.”

title: Claude-tuned Stockfish pushes a 1995-era 200 MHz Pentium Pro to nearly 3,200 Elo
summary: Anthropic engineer Nicholas Carlini used Claude to adapt chess-engine code to a 200 MHz Pentium Pro with 64 MB of RAM, pushing it to nearly 3,200 Elo at 30 seconds per move, Chip Dispatch reported on November 23, 2026, citing Tom’s Hardware. He first had Claude add modern features to Crafty, a 1996 engine that scored 2,000 Elo at one second per move on the old machine; the modified version reached 3,000 at 10 seconds. He then had Claude modify Stockfish to use 32-bit arithmetic instead of 64-bit and fit its workspace inside the 64 MB of memory. After several optimization passes, Stockfish reached 2,850 Elo at one second, 3,100 at 10 seconds and almost 3,200 at 30 seconds, about 400 points above Garry Kasparov’s peak near 2,800, which under the Elo comparison means nine wins in ten. These are rating estimates, not results from a real match, Chip Dispatch noted. The point: software efficiency rather than clock speed made the difference. Carlini made the bot playable through a link on his blog post.

title: A boy’s wish becomes Walker’s Imaginarium, the first museum built inside a children’s hospital, in New Orleans
summary: A New Orleans children’s hospital has opened the world’s first museum incorporated into a hospital, fulfilling the wish of a boy who longed for a place to escape during treatment, Good News Network reported on November 22, 2026. Walker Beery was diagnosed with pediatric brain cancer in August 2019 and fought it for two years at the hospital now called Manning Family Children’s; before he died, he and his family started the foundation Kids Join The Fight. Walker’s Imaginarium is a 15,000-square-foot museum with Louisiana themes: dancing to Cajun music, exploring a bayou, joining a Mardi Gras parade, a crawfish boil on a front porch, and a nine-hole mini-golf course with an oversized alligator. It was designed for a range of physical, sensory and medical needs, so kids in wheelchairs can play mini-golf and foosball, and it was funded entirely by donations. “Every child who finds a moment of escape, every family that experiences joy together carries Walker’s dream forward,” said his dad, Taylor. Limited outside visitors can buy daily tickets online.

title: A pub owner lights up his English town with 10,000 holiday lights just to make people smile
summary: A pub owner in Knaresborough, England, is spending around $6,000 on materials and electricity for a festive light display meant to lift locals’ spirits after a tough year of soaring living costs, Good News Network reported on November 21, 2026. “I just wanted to do something nice to make people smile,” said Christian Ogley, 34, who owns Blind Jack’s pub in the historic North Yorkshire town above the River Nidd. With seven staff members and regulars, he spent a week installing the display on his two-story pub: a 16-foot tree centerpiece built from wood and tarpaulin, white lights imitating falling snow and huge red ribbons, with more than 10,000 lights that cost about £2.50 a day to run. He began sketching the design in January on the back of beer mats, inspired by holiday displays he saw in New York City and Ireland. “It has given them something positive to talk about,” he said. He still plans to add two seven-foot nutcrackers and hopes it becomes a yearly tradition.

title: Look east tonight: the Beaver Moon kicks off three supermoons in a row
summary: The next three full moons will all be supermoons, and the first, the Beaver Moon, is set to dazzle tonight and tomorrow, Good News Network reported on November 23, 2026. Its brightest moment comes at 9:40 a.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, but nights on either side will look almost as full. Supermoons don’t look much bigger high in the sky; it’s near the horizon, framed by trees and houses, that an optical illusion makes them look huge, so the article suggests dressing warmly and stepping into an open area in early twilight to catch moonrise in the eastern sky. The name comes from the time when beavers head to their dens; the Dakota and Lakota call it the Deer Rutting Moon, the Cree the Frost Moon, and the Tlingit the Digging, or Scratching, Moon. A supermoon happens when the full Moon reaches perigee, its closest point to Earth. December’s Cold Moon will be the biggest of the three, and January’s Wolf Moon follows, all “perfect reasons to brave the cold and get out in nature.”

title: Board Game Basement invites teens and adults to the Main Library tonight
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s Main Library hosts Board Game Basement on Monday, November 23, 2026, from 5:30 to 7:45 p.m. in the second-floor Conference Room, according to the library’s event calendar. “Saunter down to the basement to enjoy board games and make new friends,” the listing says. “Feel free to bring your own games.” The program is for ages 14 and up, with more sessions listed on November 30, December 21 and December 28. Families with younger kids have options earlier in the day: the calendar lists “Santa Claus is Coming to Town!” visits at the South Regional Library from 10 a.m. to noon and at the West Regional Library from 1 to 2 p.m., where “Children will be able to take a picture with Santa using their parent's own phone, then join us for a craft!” Those visits are for ages 0 to 18, and families are welcome.

title: Teens can plant a real Thanksgiving cactus at the North Regional Library on Tuesday
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s North Regional Library hosts a Thanksgiving Cactus Craft on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, from 3 to 4 p.m. at the Carencro Welcome Center, according to the library’s event calendar. “Decorate a small pot and plant a real Thanksgiving cactus,” the listing says. “Keep it for yourself or make it a gift. All supplies provided.” The program is for ages 12 to 18, and registration is required, opening two weeks before the program date. It makes a hands-on, low-key way for teens to make a living holiday gift during the short school week before Thanksgiving.

title: Sensory Playtime for babies and toddlers comes to the West Regional Library on Wednesday
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s West Regional Library hosts Sensory Playtime on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, from 10 to 11 a.m. in the WRL Large Meeting Room, according to the library’s event calendar. “Babies and toddlers can have fun exploring various activities in this sensory play zone,” the listing says. The program is for ages 0 to 4, offering a morning outing for little ones on the day before Thanksgiving. The same morning, the calendar also lists Stay & Play at the South Regional Library at 10 a.m. and Family Storytime at the East Regional Library at 9:30 a.m.

title: Eat Dessert First: teens bake homemade cookies at the Main Library the day before Thanksgiving
summary: The Lafayette Public Library’s Main Library hosts Eat Dessert First on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, from 4 to 5 p.m. in the first-floor Teen Conference Room, according to the library’s event calendar. “The big feast is tomorrow. But life is uncertain so come to the library and make homemade cookies with us today!” the listing says. The program is for ages 12 to 18, a sweet send-off into the holiday for teens on the last day of programs before Thanksgiving, when the library calendar shows no events from Thursday, November 26, through Sunday, November 29.
